choices.content: Align one leg of the set square with \(l\), slide the set square along \(l\) until the other leg passes through point \(P\), and then draw a line along that leg.
Align the hypotenuse of the set square with \(l\), and draw a line through point \(P\) in the direction of the hypotenuse.
Draw any line through point \(P\), then use a protractor to measure that its angle with \(l\) is approximately \(90^\circ\).
Place the vertex of an acute angle of the set square at point \(P\), then draw a line along the hypotenuse.

question.prompt: Which is the correct method for using a set square to draw a perpendicular to line \(l\) through a point \(P\) outside \(l\)?

solutions.explanation: When one leg of the set square coincides with \(l\), the other leg is perpendicular to \(l\). Slide the set square until the other leg passes through \(P\), then draw along it. The resulting line passes through \(P\) and is perpendicular to \(l\).
solutions.title: Align and slide the set square
